title: Verdant Hex 01 is live: 485 hex tiles, 6 terrains with every edge, and Godot paints them
body:
Verdant Hex 01: Hex Terrain is out, at $5.99. It is the first hex pack in the Verdant series: 485 pixel art tiles on a 32x32 pointy-top hex grid, in one locked palette of 52 colours.

What is in it

  • 6 terrains: grass, plains, desert, snow, sea, ice, with 24 fill tiles.
  • 315 edge tiles. A hex has six neighbours, so one terrain meeting another takes 63 shapes, and all 63 ship for each of the 5 terrains laid over grass.
  • 128 road and river tiles, 64 each, one for every way a route can leave a hex.
  • 18 feature tiles: forest, pine forest, hills, snowy hills, mountains, village, castle, watchtower, ruins.
  • A finished 18x13 sample map as a PNG and a Tiled .tmx, a Godot 4 TileSet, and nine Tiled tilesets.

Three things we changed after looking at the map

  • The sea drew a sand beach on the snowy coast. Pack ice is now its own terrain, laid over the sea, so snow meets an ice edge.
  • River junctions read as pinwheels because every branch left the centre already curving. The branches now leave straight and bend between hexes.
  • The snowy hills read as clouds. They now have a rocky body with a snow cap.

Tested in the engines

In a blank Godot 4.7.2 project, following the Readme step by step rebuilt the shipped sample map cell for cell, with Godot's own painter choosing every edge tile. One thing the test found: Godot only draws edges into cells that already hold a tile of the same set, so each terrain layer gets a "Blank (paint first)" pass. The Readme says so up front. Tiled's own renderer matched the shipped map on all 179,712 pixels.

RPG Maker MZ cannot draw hex maps, so this pack has no MZ importer.

AI disclosure: the tiles come from a procedural pixel art engine whose code was written with AI assistance. Graphics and Code are tagged yes.
